content:
The image shows a corn ear held in hand. Key observations:
- Damage concentrated at the **tip of the ear**
- **White to light grayish-white fungal mycelium** visible at the tip
- Kernels at the tip appear **brownish, rotted, and shriveled**
- Some pinkish discoloration on damaged kernels
- Healthy yellow kernels on the lower portion of the ear
- No red/pink mold coloring as prominent as Gibberella would show
- No olive-green powdery mass (ruling out Aspergillus)
- Damage starts at tip, not base (ruling out Diplodia)

The tip-localized white to pinkish fungal growth with rotted/shriveled kernels is most consistent with **Fusarium ear rot**. The white mycelium and tip-first infection pattern are classic. The pinkish tinge on some kernels further supports Fusarium over Diplodia (base) or Gibberella (more distinctly red/pink mold).
